correctness.rationale: The six explicit graph-edge families imply a 5-regular 12-vertex antipodal graph with distance levels (1,5,5,1); its 30 distance-two edges are another icosahedron under an explicit bijection. The other six complement edges are precisely the antipodal matching, none in an independent triangle. Consequently Ind(I) is exactly a 2-sphere with six attached one-cells. The pair long exact sequence gives a canonical integral isomorphism H1 to oriented antipodal-edge lattice and hence to the anti-invariant vertex lattice; H2 is the sphere orientation line. The antipodal Lefschetz computation and fixed-vertex trace formula establish the full 120-element character and rational W6 decomposition. The standalone verifier checks every finite graph/symmetry premise. No finite experiment is substituted for a general/infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The regular icosahedron is a canonical 12-vertex antipodal polyhedron. The theorem identifies a natural complete integral G-lattice, not merely an Euler characteristic or rank, and explains its topology by a geometric distance-two sphere with attached diameters. It determines the full rational icosahedral module and contrasts rotation invariance with inversion reversal. That precise equivariant structure is motivated by the polyhedral symmetry, and no paper-sized downstream result is required for this self-contained canonical case.
